text:
A: Hello? Can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Alright. Callum.
A: Tracey. Where are you then?
B: Wolverhampton. I'm a student, before you ask. Computer science.
A: I wasn't gonna ask. You do look like a student though, sorry, but you do.
B: Is it the laundry basket?
A: It's the laundry basket. My son's room was exactly like that till he moved out. Dean. He's twenty-seven now, lives in Romford with his girlfriend, and I bet her flat's spotless cos she won't have it.
B: Yeah, that's my girlfriend as well. Them folders on the shelf are hers. Them're the only tidy bit.
A: Sounds about right. So what you gonna do with it, the computers?
B: IT support or testing, something like that. Birmingham or round here. Anything that's not nights. I did two years on nights at a warehouse off the M6 before uni and I'm not going back to that.
A: No, I don't blame you. Nights ruin you. Steve, my husband, he did nights for a bit and he was like a zombie.
B: What do you do?
A: Kitchen assistant. Primary school canteen.
B: My mum does that. School kitchen, in Wednesfield.
A: Does she? Then she'll know all about it. Is her back alright?
B: Her feet, mostly. And the cook. She's always got something to say about the cook.
A: There's always something with the cook. I fell out with one, cos she was reheating stuff she shouldn't, and I went to the manager. Then I lay awake half the night thinking I'd gone too far. But it's kids' food, you know, you can't have that. You can't.
B: Nah, fair. My mum'd say exactly the same.
A: Tell her from me, she's right, whatever it is.
B: Ha. I will. She'll like that.
A: And we ran out of jacket potatoes again this week. Every week. They don't order enough and it's me at the hatch getting the faces.
B: The kids give you faces?
A: The kids and the teachers. The teachers are worse.
B: What's your husband do then?
A: Van driver, builders' merchant. His van broke down on the A13 last week, so that was a lovely afternoon.
B: My dad drives a van. Parcels. His back's going a bit, to be honest.
A: Oh, that's hard. You do worry about them, don't you.
B: Yeah. Anyway.
A: Do you watch much telly?
B: Whatever Jade puts on. Crime documentaries, mostly. She loves them.
A: Oh, me too. I watched one last week about a man in Essex and I didn't sleep. Steve said turn it off and I said no, I need to know what happened.
B: That's the thing with them, innit, you can't stop.
A: You can't. Do yous eat proper, the two of you, or is it all takeaways?
B: Bit of both. We live above a takeaway, so the flat smells of chips every night, which doesn't help.
A: I wouldn't mind that, I have a takeaway every Friday anyway.
B: It gets old, trust me.
